top_signals.title: U.S. Opens New Front in Campaign to Cut Off Iran’s Supply Routes
top_signals.summary: The US military is expanding its efforts to disrupt Iran's supply networks beyond the naval blockade of its ports, turning its attention to the country's land borders and the Caspian Sea. On November 7, the US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the creation of Task Force Iron Gate, an internal team of approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida. It will coordinate with other US government agencies to prevent Iran from using its land borders and the Caspian Sea to transport advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies,…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: TTF Gas Bounces Back to 86 Euros as Hormuz Risks Resurface
top_signals.summary: Following a 7% dip on Monday, European benchmark natural gas prices rebounded on Tuesday morning in Amsterdam amid continued attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran targeting U.S. bases in Bahrain, and forecasts of a cold spell in large parts of Europe beginning later this week. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, rose by 2% as of 8:00 a.m. in Amsterdam on Tuesday, to $94.61 (86 euros) per megawatt-hour (MWh).
